dedupe_keys.name: rami monitoring of gold mining in the peruvian amazon mining deforestation alerts 2022 2023 acca and servir amazonia

description: Alerts of forest loss from gold mining in the southern Peruvian Amazon for 2022 and 2023, from the Monitoring of Gold Mining in the Peruvian Amazon (RAMI) service. The Dataverse record says RAMI uses Sentinel-1 radar imagery, cloud computing and the Omnibus Q-test change detection algorithm to flag potential new mining fronts in priority areas, such as buffer zones of protected areas and native communities, and notes more than 100,000 hectares of primary forest lost to gold mining in three decades. It was produced by Conservación Amazónica (ACCA) with SERVIR Amazonia, released on 19 September 2024 as version 1.0, with alert composites for 2022 and 2023 (zip files of about 68 and 90 KB) and a CSV of index changes, free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is the southern Peruvian Amazon. Caveats: alerts mark potential mining deforestation for follow-up and are not verified events, and only two years are in this release. For simulation it gives near-real-time mining disturbance events for exposure and enforcement studies, and for mercury and water contamination pathways. A related catalogue record is the Maus global mining polygons dataset.
